title: Startrails over the VLT platform
caption: Star trails over the VLT platform, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Long star trails run through the sky above the telescope platform at ESO's Paranal Observatory, where the Auxiliary Telescopes stand. The picture was built from a long series of night-time exposures by Babak Tafreshi.

The trails show the apparent motion of the sky. The stars only seem to travel. The real movement belongs to Earth, which spins on its axis and carries the observatory and the camera with it. Through the night, that spin makes every star appear to sweep slowly across the sky.

A single short exposure would catch each star as a dot. Stacking many exposures joins those dots into smooth arcs, turning a whole stretch of the night into one image. The ground turns along with the camera, so only the distant sky records the motion.

understand.summary: This is a series of night-time photographs taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal and combined into one image. The exposure settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. The trails appear only because many exposures were combined.

explore: The Auxiliary Telescopes are the smaller telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope, housed on the same summit platform as the four large Unit Telescopes.
alt: Star trails in the night sky above the Auxiliary Telescopes on an observatory platform.
